correctness.rationale: At Q(x)=s≠0, the dot-product constraint fixes the x-component of y and leaves a binary form of determinant class s, so the two distinct slice counts differ by qχ(−s) exactly when the discriminant vanishes. At nonzero isotropic x, use a hyperbolic pair and a third vector whose norm is in the class −1 (the full determinant is a square): unequal radii fix a nonzero hyperbolic coordinate and leave q solutions, while equal radii reduce to counting square roots times q. This same splitting gives q²+qχ(−s) vectors at norm s≠0 and q²−1 nonzero isotropic vectors. Mixed roots, when present, are a(1±√(b/a))², both in the class of a. Substituting 4a and 4b into the mixed discriminant gives exactly the two ninefold collisions for distinct nonzero radii; both must be counted if both occur. Squaring the convolution gives the three energy polynomials: the linear correction uses (q−σ)(q²+qσ)=q(q²−1); the squared correction includes the overlaps. After normalization the two displayed difference polynomials are strictly positive for q≥11; the additional H term is nonnegative. The exact small-field comparisons and all equality counts follow, including characteristic three and the double collision at q=5. Orthogonality and S=−S give the claimed fourth-moment/return identity.
